      "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman \u00a74 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.\n- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` \u2014 no defeq walls anywhere in this file).\n- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) \u2014 `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.\n\n**Caveat 1 \u2014 pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/\u00e9tale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now \u2014 record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.\n\n**Caveat 2 \u2014 `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free \u2124/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, \u00e9tale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient \u27e8sorry\u27e9` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.",

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

     8	/-!
     9	# Pair-transition maps in the finite-stage Picard atlas
    10	
    11	The ordered overlaps `U ∩ V` and `V ∩ U` in the exact separably closed Picard atlas are
    12	canonically identified by restriction along `inf_comm`.  This file adds those transition
    13	maps to the already descended restriction legs and spreads the entire finite family out over
    14	one common finite subextension.  At that stage the restriction legs are open immersions and
    15	the two transition directions are inverse.
    16

    18	legs, and constructing their `t'` maps and cyclic cocycle is the next boundary.
    19	-/

    36	/-! ## Exact pair transitions -/
    37	
    38	/-- The finite family of ordered pairs indexing overlap-transition maps. -/
    39	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex :=

    42	/-- The source ring of the transition indexed by `(U, V)` is the reversed overlap ring. -/
    43	def Pic0FiniteStageTransitionSource (p : Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex C) :
    44	    Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C :=
    45	  Sum.inr (p.2, p.1)
    46	
    47	/-- The target ring of the transition indexed by `(U, V)` is the forward overlap ring. -/
    48	def Pic0FiniteStageTransitionTarget (p : Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex C) :
    49	    Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C :=
    50	  Sum.inr p
    51	
    52	/-- The algebra map underlying the canonical transition from the reversed ordered overlap
    53	to the forward ordered overlap.  On schemes, `Spec.map` reverses this direction. -/
    54	noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageTransition
    55	    (p : Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex C) :
    56	    Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Pic0FiniteStageTransitionSource C p) →ₐ[k]
    57	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Pic0FiniteStageTransitionTarget C p) := by
    58	  rcases p with ⟨U, V⟩
    59	  let J := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1
    60	  letI : J.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨J.hom⟩
    61	  have hUVVU : U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 ≤ V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 := by
    62	    rw [inf_comm]

    64	    { J.left.resHom hUVVU with
    65	      commutes' := fun r =>
    66	        J.left.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k (homOfLE hUVVU).op r }

    68	/-- Reversing an exact pair transition gives its inverse. -/

    78	      (show V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 ≤ U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 by rw [inf_comm]))
    79	      (((pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.resHom
    80	        (show U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 ≤ V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 by rw [inf_comm])) x) = x

    83	/-! ## One finite family of restrictions and transitions -/
    84	
    85	/-- A finite index type containing every restriction leg and every pair transition. -/
    86	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex :=

    89	/-- Source-ring tag for the combined finite family. -/

    91	    Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C → Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C

    95	/-- Target-ring tag for the combined finite family. -/

    97	    Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C → Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C

   101	/-- The exact combined family: restrictions on the left summand and pair transitions on the

   108	  · exact pic0FiniteStageRestriction C i

   112	-- The quotient presentation creates a dependent module instance for every ring tag.
   113	/-- The chosen finite-presentation model ring at a further finite subextension. -/
   114	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageModelRing
   115	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
   116	    (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
   117	    (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C → ℕ)
   118	    (relation : ∀ j, Fin (m j) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
   119	    (M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k)
   120	    (j : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C) : Type u :=
   121	  M.1 ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
   122	    (n j) (m j) (relation j)

   124	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
   125	-- Both dependent tensor-product instances must elaborate before the conjugated map.
   126	/-- The exact combined-family map transported to the ambient tensor-product models. -/
   127	noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap
   128	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
   129	    (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
   130	    (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C → ℕ)
   131	    (relation : ∀ j, Fin (m j) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
   132	    (e : ∀ j,
   133	      k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
   134	        Pic0FiniteStageRing C j)
   135	    (q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C) :
   136	    k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
   137	        (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   138	        (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   139	        (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)) →ₐ[k]
   140	      k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
   141	        (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
   142	        (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
   143	        (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)) :=
   144	  (e (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)).symm.toAlgHom.comp
   145	    ((pic0FiniteStageMap C q).comp
   146	      (e (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)).toAlgHom)

   149	-- The source and target quotient algebras depend on the ordered chart pair.
   150	/-- The transported ambient transitions in opposite directions are inverse. -/
   151	theorem pic0FiniteStageTransportedTransition_inverse
   152	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
   153	    (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
   154	    (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C → ℕ)
   155	    (relation : ∀ j, Fin (m j) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
   156	    (e : ∀ j,
   157	      k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
   158	        Pic0FiniteStageRing C j)
   159	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   160	    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e (Sum.inr (V, U))).comp
   161	        (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e (Sum.inr (U, V))) =
   162	      AlgHom.id k
   163	        (k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
   164	          (n (Sum.inr (V, U))) (m (Sum.inr (V, U)))
   165	          (relation (Sum.inr (V, U)))) := by
   166	  change
   167	    ((e (Sum.inr (V, U))).symm.toAlgHom.comp
   168	        ((pic0FiniteStageTransition C (V, U)).comp
   169	          (e (Sum.inr (U, V))).toAlgHom)).comp
   170	        ((e (Sum.inr (U, V))).symm.toAlgHom.comp
   171	          ((pic0FiniteStageTransition C (U, V)).comp
   172	            (e (Sum.inr (V, U))).toAlgHom)) = _
   173	  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
   174	  intro x
   175	  change
   176	    (e (Sum.inr (V, U))).symm
   177	      (pic0FiniteStageTransition C (V, U)
   178	        ((e (Sum.inr (U, V)))
   179	          ((e (Sum.inr (U, V))).symm
   180	            (pic0FiniteStageTransition C (U, V)
   181	              ((e (Sum.inr (V, U))) x))))) = x
   182	  rw [(e (Sum.inr (U, V))).apply_symm_apply]
   183	  have htransition :=
   184	    DFunLike.congr_fun (pic0FiniteStageTransition_inverse C U V)
   185	      ((e (Sum.inr (V, U))) x)
   186	  calc
   187	    _ = (e (Sum.inr (V, U))).symm ((e (Sum.inr (V, U))) x) := by
   188	      exact congrArg (e (Sum.inr (V, U))).symm htransition
   189	    _ = x := (e (Sum.inr (V, U))).symm_apply_apply x

   192	-- The conclusion contains one dependent quotient-algebra instance for every finite tag.
   193	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   194	-- The simultaneous descent and equation reflection require a larger elaboration budget.
   195	/-- All exact restriction and pair-transition maps have simultaneous models over one finite
   196	subextension.  The restriction legs remain open immersions, and opposite transition maps
   197	are inverse at that same finite stage. -/
   198	theorem exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTransition_models
   199	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] :
   200	    ∃ (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
   201	      (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C → ℕ)
   202	      (relation : ∀ j, Fin (m j) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
   203	      (e : ∀ j,
   204	        k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
   205	          Pic0FiniteStageRing C j),
   206	      ∃ (M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k)
   207	        (mapM : ∀ q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
   208	          Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
   209	              (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
   210	            Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
   211	              (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)),
   212	        (∀ q,
   213	          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
   214	              (AlgHom.id L.1
   215	                (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
   216	                  (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
   217	                  (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
   218	                  (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp

   220	            ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
   221	              L.1).comp
   222	              (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val

   224	                  (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
   225	                    (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   226	                    (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   227	                    (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))))) ∧
   228	        (∀ i : Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionIndex C,
   229	          IsOpenImmersion
   230	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (mapM (Sum.inl i)).toRingHom))) ∧

     8	/-!

    10	
    11	This file isolates the elementary algebra behind finite-stage maps.  An algebra map can
    12	be extended along a scalar map, and the cancellation equivalence for a tower identifies
    13	that extension with any ambient map which commutes with the direct scalar extension.
    14	-/

    22	namespace AlgebraicJacobian

    26	/-- Scalar extension of an algebra map.  This is the map-level form of
    27	`scalarExtensionMap`, whose special case induced by an algebra structure is recorded
    28	separately in the pushout base-change file. -/
    29	def scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom {R K A B : Type u}
    30	    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    31	    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    32	    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    33	    (K ⊗[R] A) →ₐ[K] (K ⊗[R] B) :=
    34	  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id K K) f

    36	/-- `scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom` sends a pure tensor by applying the original map to
    37	its algebra factor. -/
    38	@[simp]
    39	theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tmul {R K A B : Type u}
    40	    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    41	    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    42	    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (c : K) (a : A) :
    43	    scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) f (c ⊗ₜ[R] a) =
    44	      c ⊗ₜ[R] f a := by
    45	  simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

    47	/-- Scalar extension of a map is natural in a tower of scalar rings. -/
    48	theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower {F L K A B : Type u}
    49	    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    50	    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    51	    [Algebra F A] [Algebra F B]
    52	    (f : A →ₐ[F] B) :
    53	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
    54	        (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
    55	        ((scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := F) (K := L) f).restrictScalars F) =
    56	      ((scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := F) (K := K) f).restrictScalars F).comp
    57	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
    58	          (AlgHom.id F A)) := by
    59	  ext x
    60	  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]
    61	  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]
    62	
    63	/-- Scalar extension preserves composition of algebra maps. -/
    64	@[simp]
    65	theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_comp {R K A B D : Type u}
    66	    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B] [Semiring D]
    67	    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R D]
    68	    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : B →ₐ[R] D) :

    70	        (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) f) =

    85	/-- Cancellation on a tensor whose right factor is itself a scalar extension. -/
    86	theorem cancelBaseChange_tmul_baseChange {F L K A : Type u}
    87	    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [CommRing A]
    88	    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    89	    [Algebra F A] (c : K) (x : L ⊗[F] A) :
    90	    Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K A (c ⊗ₜ[L] x) =
    91	      c • Algebra.TensorProduct.map
    92	        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A) x := by
    93	  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    94	  | zero => simp
    95	  | add x y hx hy =>
    96	      rw [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy, map_add, smul_add]
    97	  | tmul l a =>
    98	      simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange_tmul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]
    99	
   100	/-- Cancellation is natural for maps between two base changes from `F` to `L` which

   102	theorem cancelBaseChange_naturality {F L K A B : Type u}
   103	    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]

    40	  have e_inv_fst : e.inv ≫ a = pullback.fst iU iV := by

    42	    exact IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv_comp hW
    43	      (pullback.isLimit iU iV) WalkingCospan.left

    46	      (pullback.fst (iU ≫ f) g ≫ iU) iV
    47	      (pullback.snd g (iU ≫ f) ≫ iU) iV
    48	      (pullbackSymmetry (iU ≫ f) g).hom (𝟙 V) (𝟙 X)

    53	      (pullback.fst iU iV ≫ (iU ≫ f)) g
    54	      (a ≫ iU ≫ f) g
